title: Adab of sleep
hookLine: the one thing no one can do on purpose, and the remembrance that goes with it

cards: Lights off. Phone face down. And then the one thing in the day nobody can do on purpose: fall asleep.
You can't push your way into it. You can only lie down and let go. The Qur'an treats that letting go as no small thing.
In surah al-Zumar, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah receiveth (men's) souls at the time of their death, and that (soul) which dieth not (yet) in its sleep." Every night, something is handed over.

teach.b: Start with al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, in Sahih al-Bukhari.

The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, told him, in paraphrase: when you go to your bed, make wudu as you would for prayer, lie down on your right side, and say a short du'a handing yourself over to Allah.
Make it your last words, he said. If you die that night, you die on the fitrah, the natural state.
The body washed, laid down a particular way, and the last words of the day chosen, not left to whatever was on the screen. Some of this you met on day one hundred thirty-six.

Then 'A'ishah adds what she saw night after night, also in Bukhari: he cupped his hands, blew into them lightly, and recited the three short surahs at the end of the Qur'an, al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas, the three quls, each beginning with qul, say.
Then he wiped his hands over as much of his body as he could, starting with his head and face, three times. Last, two sentences from Hudhayfah, in Bukhari.

teach.h: IN YOUR NAME I DIE AND I LIVE.
teach.b: Lying down: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. Waking, in paraphrase: praise to Allah, who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the rising. Sleep, a small dying.
Waking, a small rising. The verse from al-Zumar, folded into two lines a person can say in the dark.

how: Muslims follow the Prophet's bedtime practice: making wudu, lying on the right side, reciting al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas into cupped hands and wiping over the body, and saying "bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya" before sleep.

o: washing, lying on the right side, remembering Allah
staying awake all night in prayer instead of sleep
rules for how many hours a believer should sleep

games.q: the adab of sleep — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an speaks of sleep as a taking of the soul
al-Zumar: Allah receives souls at death, and the soul that has not died, in its sleep.
the bedtime surahs were recited once, quickly
'A'ishah reports he blew into cupped hands, recited them, and wiped over his body, three times.
the waking words thank Allah for life after sleep
praise to Allah, who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the rising.

games.q: al-Bara' has made wudu and lain down on his right side. the Prophet tells him what his last words of the night should be. what are they?
o: a short du'a handing himself over to Allah.
games.why: make it your last words, the Prophet said: if you die that night, you die on the fitrah.

practice: Rehearse tonight: water on your hands and face, wudu or simply washing, then lying down on your right side.
If you know al-Ikhlas, say it slowly in your mind, qul huwa Allahu ahad, and if you pray, plan for your last words to be bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya, in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
If you don't, choose one thing from today to set down before you sleep, and see yourself setting it down.

wordCard.voice: Adab of sleep. The manners of lying down: wudu, the right side, the three quls, and a last word of remembrance before the day lets go. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: sleep with remembrance. Each night a small dying, each morning a small rising. Tomorrow, the manners of learning.
